title: Compare Sums of Bitonic Parts
summary: Given a bitonic array of length n, split it into an ascending part from index 0 to the peak element and a descending part from the peak element to index n-1.
statement: Given a bitonic array of length n, split it into an ascending part from index 0 to the peak element and a descending part from the peak element to index n-1. Return 0 if the ascending part's sum is greater, 1 if the descending part's sum is greater, and -1 if both sums are equal. A bitonic array strictly increases to a peak and then strictly decreases.
constraints: nums strictly increases to one peak and then strictly decreases; either side may contain only the peak.
Both part sums include the peak.
Return 0 when the ascending sum is larger, 1 when the descending sum is larger, and -1 on a tie.
reference_solution:
def compare_bitonic_part_sums(nums):
    peak=max(range(len(nums)),key=nums.__getitem__)
    left=sum(nums[:peak+1]);right=sum(nums[peak:])
    return -1 if left==right else 0 if left>right else 1

def compare_bitonic_part_sums(nums):

hints: Locate the unique maximum, which is the peak.
Sum through the peak from each side, deliberately including it twice across the two comparisons.
Compare the two totals with the specified three-way codes.
The bitonic invariant makes the maximum index the exact split point.
editorial: The bitonic invariant makes the maximum index the exact split point.
